title: Big Ideas For Small Bathrooms
bodyHtml:
With a little bit of imagination and creativity, designing your ideal bathroom is not far from reach!

First and foremost, it's important to have a good grasp of the big idea. Whether you want to create an indulgent spa-like experience, chic boutique hotel or even the cosy country-house feel, the challenge is to select beautiful and functional bathware for the available space.

In planning for your ideal bathroom, the toughest questions you'll need to address include size versus style, functionality versus aesthetic and ready-to-install versus custom made. You'll also need to carefully consider the budget you've set aside for the makeover too.

Fortunately, you're not short of alternatives. From above counter to under countertop basins, floor-mounted toilets to wall-hung toilets and mounted bathroom towel rails and portable towel rails, the choices are endless. In this article, we'll help you go BIG on ideas for your perfect bathroom, whatever the size may be.

1. The Bathroom Basin

Here, you're faced with 3 decisions: position, size and design.

The bathroom basin is the 'epi-centre' of the bathroom. It's where you'll be spending most of your time. Whether it's that one last look before you head out or where you keep your daily routine essentials, there is lots to think about in the design of your bathroom sink. To a large extent, it defines the character of the room.

As far as location is concerned, the bathroom sink should not get in the way of the door opening or closing. You shouldn't have to squeeze yourself in and out of the bathroom because of the location of the basin. So, whether it is situated in the corner or elsewhere, be mindful of the central role the bathroom basin plays.

Size matters if you have a small bathroom. But with the plethora of design styles available today, you don't have to sacrifice the aesthetic appeal of a vanity basin for a functional small bathroom basin. There are different sizes that can fit your available space, and whether you choose to install a countertop vanity basin, above or under the countertop, you're only limited by your imagination and practical considerations.

"Wall Hung Basins work best when you are really tight on space"

While it may be less common in Australian homes, wall hung basin like our collection Spy, are a great way to capitalize on space with smart designed basins that have a short projection and built-in shelves. Some basins like our Shard X Mini allow you to attach a towel rail saving you space whilst increasing functionality at the same time. Perhaps wall hung basins work best when you are really tight on space. But as mentioned at the onset, a small space should not prevent you from exploring big ideas for your bathroom.

Choosing to float your vanity bathroom sink can free up floor space. In addition, it'll make the bathroom appear less cluttered. You can use the space beneath for a variety of things. For example, choosing to place rolled-up towels underneath can give your bathroom a spa-like feel. A floating vanity bathroom sink helps make cleaning and maintenance easier too.

2. The Toilet

It's the next most commonly used amenity in the bathroom, after the basin. With the abundance of options available here, you are again spoilt for choice. The variety of designs and sizes means there is one that will fit your desired style perfectly.

If you're after a minimalist look, consider hiding the cistern and all the components that comes with it in the wall. This means that only the flush button is visible, saving you a heap of space. Keep in mind that you'll need to be cautious of the occasional breakdowns that may occur. Ensuring a plumber can easily access the cistern concealed in the wall will be a priority during the design stage.

Coupled with the need to save space, you can consider wall hung toilets too. Like floating vanity sinks, the floor space you gain can avoid a cluttered or busy look. And like the former, it makes cleaning and maintenance of your bathroom easier as well.

The rimless toilet is fast becoming a standard in any modern bathroom. They are increasingly popular and affordable too. Rimless toilets tick many boxes - they are more hygienic, easier to clean and maintain, and they stay cleaner for longer.

3. Bathroom Accessories

Mirrors

The right sized mirror suitably positioned can 'add' to the size of your bathroom. It doesn't have to serve just a functional purpose. And you can have more than one. Aside from placing it above the vanity/sink, you can add another on the back of the door. This will likely be a full-length mirror.

Towels

You can never have too many towels, but unfortunately, we must always consider storage space. Thanks to the influence of day-spa style bathrooms, towels are not only functional but they are aesthetic pieces in the bathroom today as well. And because of their material, they can add warmth to your bathroom. So, make sure you have towel rails conveniently located, for example, next to the sink and toilet as well as beneath a floating vanity sink, if you opt for one of these!

Storage

It's nice to be able to store all-bath necessities, for example, shower gel, soap and shampoo, in your bathroom. But when you're short on space, this isn't always an option. So, if you wish to store them in the bathroom, you'll need to get creative! As well as looking at how you can use the space underneath the sink, think about your walls as well - is there space above the door for a shelf? Could you add hooks to the walls or baskets to the back of your cabinet doors? The possibilities are endless if you take the time to consider the space you have available.
